addmaths-0606-kinematic-derivatives.description: Use derivatives to calculate velocity and acceleration, find when a particle stops and explain its motion along a straight line.

sections.title: How fast is the position changing?
sections.label: Velocity

blocks.html: A displacement measures position from an origin along the chosen positive direction. Its derivative is the signed velocity \(v=\frac{\mathrm ds}{\mathrm dt}\).

figure.alt: The displacement rises, has a horizontal tangent at 2 seconds, then falls. The origin of displacement is 3 m below its maximum.
figure.caption: The displacement rises, has a horizontal tangent at 2 seconds, then falls. The origin of displacement is 3 m below its maximum.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Start by drawing the origin and the positive direction. Differentiate the formula for displacement term by term. A stationary value of the position has velocity zero. The sign of the displacement alone gives a position.

blocks.title: Find motion from a position function
blocks.prompt:
A toy train on a straight track has displacement \(s=6 t^{2} - 84 t + 4\) for \(0\le t\le 19\), where t is measured in seconds.

Find the velocity v in terms of t.
blocks.hint: Take the derivatives in order. The particle is at rest where the first derivative is zero.
blocks.solution:
Differentiate each term of the position formula. A constant term has derivative zero.

\(v=12 t - 84\)

Answer: \(12 t - 84\).

retry.feedback: Differentiate displacement once for velocity and twice for acceleration. Keep signs throughout.

blocks.html: A negative displacement puts the particle on the negative side of the origin. Its velocity may still be positive.

blocks.title: Find motion from a position function
blocks.prompt:
A toy train on a straight track has displacement \(s=\frac{t^{2}}{2} - 5 t + 5\) for \(0\le t\le 11\), where t is measured in seconds.

Find all the times at which the particle is at rest.
blocks.hint: Take the derivatives in order. The particle is at rest where the first derivative is zero.
blocks.solution:
Set the signed velocity \(t - 5\) equal to zero. Give all roots in the stated time interval.

Answer: \(t=5\).

retry.feedback: Differentiate displacement once for velocity and twice for acceleration. Keep signs throughout.

sections.label: At rest

blocks.html: Use \(v=0\) to find a time with no instantaneous motion. Check the permitted time interval and give every valid time.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Write the velocity equation, factor it where possible and solve each factor. To confirm a reversal, check the sign of velocity before and after the instant.

blocks.title: Find motion from a position function
blocks.prompt:
A battery-powered inspection device moves along a straight track. Its position in metres, measured from a fixed reference, is \(s=\frac{5 t^{3}}{3} - \frac{75 t^{2}}{2} + 270 t - 5\) for \(0\le t\le 13\), where t is measured in seconds.

Find the velocity v in terms of t.
blocks.hint: Take the derivatives in order. The particle is at rest where the first derivative is zero.
blocks.solution:
Differentiate each term of the position formula. A constant term has derivative zero.

\(v=5 t^{2} - 75 t + 270\)

Answer: \(5 t^{2} - 75 t + 270\).

retry.feedback: Differentiate displacement once for velocity and twice for acceleration. Keep signs throughout.

blocks.html: An acceleration of zero means the velocity is momentarily unchanged. The velocity may be positive, negative or zero at that time.

blocks.title: Find motion from a position function
blocks.prompt:
A battery-powered inspection device moves along a straight track. Its position in metres, measured from a fixed reference, is \(s=\frac{5 t^{3}}{3} - 25 t^{2} + 80 t + 7\) for \(0\le t\le 9\), where t is measured in seconds.

Find all the times at which the particle is at rest.
blocks.hint: Take the derivatives in order. The particle is at rest where the first derivative is zero.
blocks.solution:
Set the signed velocity \(\left(t - 8\right) \left(5 t - 10\right)\) equal to zero. Give all roots in the stated time interval.

Answer: \(t=2\text{ or }t=8\).

blocks.html: Differentiate again to obtain \(a=\frac{\mathrm dv}{\mathrm dt}=\frac{\mathrm d^2s}{\mathrm dt^2}\). It measures the change in signed velocity each second.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Find the velocity expression first. Differentiate it to obtain acceleration and evaluate it at the requested time. Retain a negative result as a signed physical quantity. Compare the signs of velocity and acceleration if asked whether speed increases.

blocks.title: Read direction from a displacement model
blocks.prompt:
A trolley moves on a straight horizontal rail. Its displacement from the marker is \(s=- \frac{5 t^{2}}{2} + 15 t - 5\), in metres, for \(0\le t\le 8\), where t is measured in seconds. Take right as positive.

Find the velocity v in terms of t.
blocks.hint: Use the rate of change of displacement to determine motion. Then compare the signed velocity and acceleration.
blocks.solution:
Differentiate the displacement expression once with respect to time.

\(v=15 - 5 t\)

Answer: \(15 - 5 t\).

retry.feedback: Direction comes from the sign of velocity. A negative displacement gives a position relative to the origin.

blocks.html: When velocity and acceleration are both negative, speed is increasing.

blocks.title: Read direction from a displacement model
blocks.prompt:

Find the acceleration at \(t=6\) and include its sign.
blocks.hint: Use the rate of change of displacement to determine motion. Then compare the signed velocity and acceleration.
blocks.solution:
Differentiate velocity to obtain \(a=-9\). The acceleration is constant for this model.

Answer: \(-9\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

blocks.html: Use \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) as the unit pattern for velocity and \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) as the pattern for acceleration. Show the derivative before substituting.

revision.body:
How fast is the position changing?

A displacement measures position from an origin along the chosen positive direction. Its derivative is the signed velocity \(v=\frac{\mathrm ds}{\mathrm dt}\).

How do I find the times at rest?

Use \(v=0\) to find a time with no instantaneous motion. Check the permitted time interval and give every valid time.

What does acceleration measure?

Differentiate again to obtain \(a=\frac{\mathrm dv}{\mathrm dt}=\frac{\mathrm d^2s}{\mathrm dt^2}\). It measures the change in signed velocity each second.

Quick worked example

A toy train on a straight track has displacement \(s=\frac{t^{2}}{2} - 5 t + 4\) for \(0\le t\le 14\), where t is measured in seconds.

Find the velocity v in terms of t.

Differentiate each term of the position formula. A constant term has derivative zero.

\(v=t - 5\)
revision.checks:
• A negative displacement puts the particle on the negative side of the origin. Its velocity may still be positive.
  • An acceleration of zero means the velocity is momentarily unchanged. The velocity may be positive, negative or zero at that time.
revision.examTip: Use \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) as the unit pattern for velocity and \(1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) as the pattern for acceleration. Show the derivative before substituting.

addmaths-0606-kinematic-integration.description: Integrate acceleration or velocity, use initial conditions to fix constants and calculate changes of position on a specified interval.

sections.title: How can I recover velocity from acceleration?
sections.label: Initial velocity

blocks.html: Integrate acceleration with respect to time. Determine the constant of integration from a known velocity, such as \(v(0)\).

figure.alt: Signed area under the velocity line gives displacement. The first triangle contributes negatively and the second positively.
figure.caption: Signed area under the velocity line gives displacement. The first triangle contributes negatively and the second positively.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Integrate every term of the acceleration and append a constant. Substitute the time and corresponding velocity to determine it. Differentiate your final velocity expression to check that it gives the original acceleration.

blocks.title: Recover initial conditions in a motion model
blocks.prompt:
A small robot moves on a straight line. For \(0\le t\le 10\) it has constant acceleration \(7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). It starts at displacement \(-5\,\mathrm{m}\) with velocity \(-32\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Find an expression for the velocity v at time t.
blocks.hint: Integrate in the order indicated by the information. Use the initial data after each integration.
blocks.solution:
An antiderivative of the acceleration is \(7 t\). Use \(v(0)=-32\) to fix the constant.

\(v=7 t - 32\)

Answer: \(7 t - 32\).

retry.feedback: Velocity and displacement can require different constants. The position at one time and a change of position are distinct quantities.

blocks.html: An initial velocity can be negative. Keep the sign when substituting the condition.

blocks.title: Recover initial conditions in a motion model
blocks.prompt:
A small robot moves on a straight line. For \(0\le t\le 11\) it has constant acceleration \(8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). It starts at displacement \(-10\,\mathrm{m}\) with velocity \(-25\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Find an expression for the displacement s from the origin at time t.
blocks.hint: Integrate in the order indicated by the information. Use the initial data after each integration.
blocks.solution:
Integrate \(8 t - 25\) to obtain the variable part. At time zero the displacement is \(-10\,\mathrm{m}\).

\(s=4 t^{2} - 25 t - 10\)

Answer: \(4 t^{2} - 25 t - 10\).

retry.feedback: Velocity and displacement can require different constants. The position at one time and a change of position are distinct quantities.

blocks.html: Integrating a known velocity gives an expression for position with its own constant. Use a stated position such as \(s(0)\) to fix that constant.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: First determine the full velocity formula. Integrate that formula, including its constant term. Then substitute the given position and time. If the particle starts at the origin, use zero as its initial position.

blocks.title: Recover initial conditions in a motion model
blocks.prompt:
A motor drives a carriage in a straight line. Its acceleration is \(a=10 t - 85\) in metres per second squared for \(0\le t\le 14\). At time zero its velocity is \(360\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and its displacement is \(-6\,\mathrm{m}\).

Find an expression for the velocity v at time t.
blocks.hint: Integrate in the order indicated by the information. Use the initial data after each integration.
blocks.solution:
An antiderivative of the acceleration is \(5 t^{2} - 85 t\). Use \(v(0)=360\) to fix the constant.

\(v=5 t^{2} - 85 t + 360\)

Answer: \(5 t^{2} - 85 t + 360\).

retry.feedback: Velocity and displacement can require different constants. The position at one time and a change of position are distinct quantities.

blocks.html: The constant in the velocity formula gets multiplied by t when you integrate. There is a new constant for displacement.

blocks.title: Recover initial conditions in a motion model
blocks.prompt:
A motor drives a carriage in a straight line. Its acceleration is \(a=22 t - 132\) in metres per second squared for \(0\le t\le 14\). At time zero its velocity is \(290\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and its displacement is \(12\,\mathrm{m}\).

Find an expression for the displacement s from the origin at time t.
blocks.hint: Integrate in the order indicated by the information. Use the initial data after each integration.
blocks.solution:
Integrate \(11 t^{2} - 132 t + 290\) to obtain the variable part. At time zero the displacement is \(12\,\mathrm{m}\).

\(s=\frac{11 t^{3}}{3} - 66 t^{2} + 290 t + 12\)

Answer: \(\frac{11 t^{3}}{3} - 66 t^{2} + 290 t + 12\).

retry.feedback: Velocity and displacement can require different constants. The position at one time and a change of position are distinct quantities.

sections.title: How can I find displacement over one interval?
sections.label: Change in position

blocks.html: Integrate signed velocity from the earlier time to the later time. By \(\int_a^b v\,\mathrm dt=s(b)-s(a)\), a fixed origin cancels out.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html: Check whether the question asks for the position at a time or the change between two times. For a change, evaluate the displacement function at both times and subtract in chronological order. A velocity graph gives the same result after adding its areas with signs.

blocks.title: Recover initial conditions in a motion model
blocks.prompt:
An automated gate moves in a straight line with velocity \(v=71 - 12 t\) in metres per second for \(0\le t\le 10\). At time zero the gate is \(4\,\mathrm{m}\) ahead of its reference marker. The positive direction is forwards.

Find an expression for the displacement s from the origin at time t.
blocks.hint: Integrate in the order indicated by the information. Use the initial data after each integration.
blocks.solution:
Integrate \(71 - 12 t\) to obtain the variable part. At time zero the displacement is \(4\,\mathrm{m}\).

\(s=- 6 t^{2} + 71 t + 4\)

Answer: \(- 6 t^{2} + 71 t + 4\).

retry.feedback: Velocity and displacement can require different constants. The position at one time and a change of position are distinct quantities.

blocks.html: A question about the displacement from the origin at a given time needs the initial position. The change over an interval does not need it.

blocks.title: Recover initial conditions in a motion model
blocks.prompt:
An automated gate moves in a straight line with velocity \(v=1 - t\) in metres per second for \(0\le t\le 12\). At time zero the gate is \(11\,\mathrm{m}\) ahead of its reference marker. The positive direction is forwards.

Find the displacement during the interval from \(5\,\mathrm{s}\) to \(12\,\mathrm{s}\).
blocks.hint: Integrate in the order indicated by the information. Use the initial data after each integration.
blocks.solution:
Use final position \(-49\,\mathrm{m}\) minus the position \(\frac{7}{2}\,\mathrm{m}\) at the start of the interval.

Answer: \(- \frac{105}{2}\,\mathrm{m}\).

retry.feedback: Velocity and displacement can require different constants. The position at one time and a change of position are distinct quantities.

blocks.html: Calculate a definite integral using the later time minus the earlier time. Include the initial value when the task gives a position to recover.

Integrating a known velocity gives an expression for position with its own constant. Use a stated position such as \(s(0)\) to fix that constant.

How can I find displacement over one interval?

Integrate signed velocity from the earlier time to the later time. By \(\int_a^b v\,\mathrm dt=s(b)-s(a)\), a fixed origin cancels out.

Quick worked example

A small robot moves on a straight line. For \(0\le t\le 12\) it has constant acceleration \(10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). It starts at displacement \(-1\,\mathrm{m}\) with velocity \(-40\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

Find an expression for the velocity v at time t.

An antiderivative of the acceleration is \(10 t\). Use \(v(0)=-40\) to fix the constant.

\(v=10 t - 40\)
revision.checks:
• An initial velocity can be negative. Keep the sign when substituting the condition.
  • The constant in the velocity formula gets multiplied by t when you integrate. There is a new constant for displacement.
revision.examTip: Calculate a definite integral using the later time minus the earlier time. Include the initial value when the task gives a position to recover.

blocks.title: Displacement and total distance
blocks.prompt: A cart moves with velocity \(v=6-2t,\quad 0\le t\le4\) metres per second. Find its signed displacement and its total distance.

retry.feedback: 8 m is the net displacement. For distance, add the length of the return leg to the length of the outward leg.

blocks.hint: Set velocity to zero. The turning time divides the graph into two triangles. Decide how each area contributes to each answer.
blocks.solution:
The cart changes direction at \(t=3\). The first part gives \(\frac12(3)(6)=9\) m. The final part gives a signed change of \(-\frac12(1)(2)=-1\) m.

The signed displacement is \(9-1=8\) m. The total distance is \(9+1=10\) m.

revision.body:
Where should I split the time interval?

Solve \(v=0\) within the model's time range. Check where the sign of v actually changes. Each change separates two directions of motion.

What does the signed integral measure?

The integral \(\int_a^b v\,\mathrm dt\) measures the net change in position. Parts of the journey in opposite directions can cancel.

How do I calculate total distance?

Total distance is the area under the speed graph. Compute \(\int_a^b |v|\,\mathrm dt\) by splitting at changes of direction, then adding the magnitudes of the separate displacements.

Quick worked example

A robot moves along a straight rail. Its velocity in metres per second is \(v=2t-4,\quad 0\le t\le5\). Find the signed displacement and the total distance travelled.

Solve \(2t-4=0\) to get \(t=2\). The robot moves in the negative direction before 2 s, then in the positive direction.

Integrate \(2t-4\) to obtain \(t^2-4t\). From 0 to 2 s the signed displacement is \([t^2-4t]_0^2=-4\) m. From 2 to 5 s it is \([t^2-4t]_2^5=9\) m.

The signed displacement is \(-4+9=5\) m. The total distance is \(|-4|+|9|=13\) m.
revision.checks: At a zero of velocity, check whether the sign changes. Add signed areas for displacement and their magnitudes for distance.
revision.examTip: Show all the direction-change times and the separate distance contributions. Label the final answer in metres.

addmaths-0606-kinematic-graphs.description: Connect and sketch displacement, distance, velocity, speed and acceleration graphs through gradients, signs and areas.

sections.title: How do the signed graphs fit together?
sections.label: Signed sketch

blocks.html: A displacement graph with gradient \(v=0\) has a horizontal tangent. An increasing velocity graph has positive acceleration, including where its velocity is negative.

figure.alt: Velocity starts below the axis. Speed reflects this initial segment above the axis. The two graphs coincide after 2 seconds.
figure.caption: Velocity starts below the axis. Speed reflects this initial segment above the axis. The two graphs coincide after 2 seconds.

blocks.title: Practise the method
blocks.html:
Calculate the endpoint values and all relevant zero crossings. Plot velocity before drawing a displacement or acceleration sketch. Use the velocity signs to find increasing and decreasing sections of displacement and use its gradient for acceleration.

Five graphs for one-dimensional motion
GraphUse this relationship
Displacement against timeGradient is velocity
Distance against timeGradient is speed
Velocity against timeGradient is acceleration and signed area is displacement
Speed against timeArea is total distance
Acceleration against timeSigned area is change in velocity

blocks.title: Link scale sketches of the motion
blocks.prompt:
A parcel on a testing rail has velocity \(v=7 t - 14\) in metres per second over \(0\le t\le 9\). Its initial displacement from the origin is \(1\,\mathrm{m}\).

Calculate the velocity when \(t=9\).
blocks.hint: Use the stated time in the velocity expression. Compare the sign of the result with the height on the velocity graph.
blocks.solution:
Substitute the final time into \(7 t - 14\). A graph of velocity keeps the sign.

Answer: \(49\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

retry.feedback: Reflect a velocity graph to obtain speed only where velocity is negative. The distance graph keeps increasing as long as the particle moves.

blocks.html: A zero on the acceleration graph marks zero velocity gradient. It can occur when the particle has non-zero signed velocity.

Answer: \(\frac{77}{2}\,\mathrm{m}\).

extraPractice.prompt:
A parcel on a testing rail has velocity \(v=25 - 5 t\) in metres per second over \(0\le t\le 13\). Its initial displacement from the origin is \(-11\,\mathrm{m}\).

Calculate the velocity when \(t=13\).
extraPractice.hint: Use the stated time in the velocity expression. Compare the sign of the result with the height on the velocity graph.
extraPractice.solution:
Substitute the final time into \(25 - 5 t\). A graph of velocity keeps the sign.

Answer: \(-40\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).

retry.feedback: Reflect a velocity graph to obtain speed only where velocity is negative. The distance graph keeps increasing as long as the particle moves.

extraPractice.title: Link scale sketches of the motion
extraPractice.prompt:
A parcel on a testing rail has velocity \(v=48 - 8 t\) in metres per second over \(0\le t\le 14\). Its initial displacement from the origin is \(-6\,\mathrm{m}\).

Find the distance travelled over the whole interval.
extraPractice.hint: Use the zero of velocity to split the graph, then add both triangle areas as positive distances.
extraPractice.solution:
The velocity graph gives signed triangular areas \(144\,\mathrm{m}\) and \(-256\,\mathrm{m}\). Add their magnitudes.

Answer: \(400\,\mathrm{m}\).

related.title: Total distance and changes of direction

glossary.definition: A labelled graph showing the relevant values, intercepts and behaviour.
The distance travelled between the given times.
Instantaneous speed, so the gradient is non-negative.

revision.body:
How do the signed graphs fit together?

A displacement graph with gradient \(v=0\) has a horizontal tangent. An increasing velocity graph has positive acceleration, including where its velocity is negative.

How do I draw the speed graph?

Speed is \(|v|\). Reflect each section of the velocity graph below the time axis to the same height above it. Leave the other parts of the graph in place.

What does the distance graph look like?

The gradient of the distance graph is \(|v|\). The graph of accumulated distance begins at zero and increases while the particle moves in either direction.

Quick worked example

A parcel on a testing rail has velocity \(v=4 t - 8\) in metres per second over \(0\le t\le 6\). Its initial displacement from the origin is \(-6\,\mathrm{m}\).

Calculate the velocity when \(t=6\).

Substitute the final time into \(4 t - 8\). A graph of velocity keeps the sign.

Answer: \(16\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\).
revision.checks:
• A zero on the acceleration graph marks zero velocity gradient. It can occur when the particle has non-zero signed velocity.
  • A negative area under velocity contributes a positive area under speed after the reflection.
revision.examTip: Label both axes and units. For a velocity graph, show any sections below the time axis before converting to speed.
